AI CLOSED-LOOP AUTONOMOUS MANUFACTURING OF BIOMEDICAL MICRO/NANOROBOTS AT THE LIMIT AI Process Control x Real-Time Metrology x Functional Manufacturing Yield This 770-page Research Working Edition develops a falsification-oriented, nonclinical architecture for AI closed-loop manufacturing of biomedical micro/nanorobots. It treats online images, process telemetry, material identity, calibrated uncertainty, controller actions, physical constraints, abstention, human intervention and independent functional qualification as distinct scientific objects. A higher yield is not accepted as autonomous improvement when the controller used extra trials, hidden expert rescue, proxy-only labels or unsafe exploration. The monograph contains 30 distinct mathematical research plates, 82 chapters, 410 single-page investigations, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 genuinely distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos. Model families include Bayesian process-state estimation, image calibration, functional pass posteriors, constrained expected improvement, Gaussian-process safe sets, OOD scores, conformal coverage, selective risk, probability calibration, drift and change-point models, barrier functions, chance constraints, violation budgets, constrained regret, sample efficiency, multi-fidelity co-kriging, causal intervention, off-policy evaluation, digital-twin discrepancy, robust MPC, epistemic uncertainty and replayable release logic. The minimum demonstrator compares a fixed recipe, preregistered DOE, logged expert tuning and a constrained AI controller using hidden resin batches under identical material, trial, time, sensing and labor budgets. Familiar, shifted and unsupported lots plus concealed sensor drift test whether the controller abstains before repair. High-confidence output on an OOD batch, any safety-constraint crossing, hidden human intervention or broken event replay is a hard veto. This is a prospective scientific architecture, not an executed clinical study. It does not claim in-body safety, therapeutic efficacy, regulatory approval or clinical benefit. DOI-linked publications support component methods and boundary conditions; they do not validate the integrated F21 manufacturing system.
